name: The Obsidian Crown
plot: A disgraced knight and a novice druid embark on a perilous journey to destroy an ancient cursed crown before a dark sorcerer can use it to resurrect an army of the dead.

characters.description: A sinister sorcerer seeking to conquer the realm.
characters.voiceDescription: Sibilant, cold, and echoing with dark magic.

dialogues.text: The rain fell in sheets, turning the dirt roads of Oakhaven into a sea of mud.
Another ale, Sir Alaric? You've been staring at the bottom of that tankard for an hour.
I lost my knighthood, Gromm. Don't call me 'Sir'. And yes, another ale.
As you wish. But drinking yourself to death won't change what happened at the capital.
It blunts the memory, which is good enough.
Suddenly, the heavy oak doors of the tavern burst open, revealing a young woman cloaked in green, gasping for breath.
Is there anyone here who can hold a sword? The shadow beasts are coming!
Shadow beasts? Girl, you've spent too much time in the woods. Those are fairy tales.
I saw them with my own eyes! They tore through the northern blockade!
Quiet down, girl. Some of us are trying to drown our miseries in peace.
You! You have a sword at your hip! Stand up and help defend this town!
I am no longer a defender of towns. Go find the local militia.
The militia is dead. Malakor's forces have already slaughtered them.
Malakor? The dark sorcerer? He's been sealed away for a century.
Not anymore. Someone broke the seal. And they stole the Obsidian Crown.
The mention of the crown brought a sudden, chilling silence to the tavern.
The Crown of the Dead... by the gods.
If Malakor has the crown, we're all already dead. Running just means dying tired.
I won't just sit here and wait for death! I am Elara of the Elder Grove, and I will fight.
A terrifying howl shattered the peace of the night. The wooden walls of the tavern shuddered.
Grab your weapons! Bar the doors!
A bar won't hold against shadow beasts. Gromm, is there a cellar exit?
Yes, out by the stables.
Everyone, into the cellar. Move!
Wait, we can't just run!
We can, and we will. Unless you want your soul ripped from your body to fuel Malakor's magic.
The tavern door splintered inwardly, and creatures made of smoke and glowing red eyes poured into the room.
Go! I'll hold them off!
I thought you didn't care!
I care about Gromm's ale! Now move!
Alaric drew his broadsword, the steel catching the dim light of the hearth.
Come on, you ugly bastards. Show me what dark magic bleeds!
Spirits of the earth, bind them! Vine and root, heed my call!
Thick vines erupted through the floorboards, entangling the shadow beasts and giving the patrons time to escape.
Druid magic. Didn't think there were any of you left.
There are a few. Come on, the vines won't hold them forever!
Alaric and Elara plunged into the rainy night, rushing out of the village.
The village is lost. We head for the mountains.
No, we head north. To the Obsidian Keep. We have to destroy the crown.
You're mad. Two people can't assault a fortress.
It's the only way to stop the dead from rising. Don't you have any honor left, knight?
My honor was stripped from me when I refused to execute innocent villagers for the King.
Then you're a good man. The realm needs good men right now.
The realm needs an army. We have a sword and some weeds.
Have faith, Alaric. The earth is with us.
They traveled through the night, the howls of the shadow beasts fading behind them.
We need to rest. Even shadow beasts lose the scent in heavy rain.
I'll make a fire. It needs to be smokeless.
Elara spoke softly to the dampened wood, and soon a small, clean flame flickered to life.
Handy trick. Who taught you that?
The Arch-Druid. Before Malakor murdered him.
I'm sorry. I didn't know.
Malakor wants the crown to conquer the realm, but to me... this is revenge for my master.
Revenge is a poisoned chalice, Elara. Drink it, and you'll find it consumes you from the inside.
And what drives you, Alaric? Why did you come with me?
To die, I suppose. Seemed like a better way to go than choking on cheap ale.
I don't believe you. Beneath that gruff exterior is a man who still wants to save the world.
Get some sleep. We have to cross the Whispering Woods tomorrow.
The next morning, a thick fog blanketed the ancient forest.
Stay close. This forest plays tricks on the mind.
I can hear voices... they sound familiar.
Elara... you failed me, Elara...
Master? Is that you?
Don't listen! Put your hands over your ears! It's the woods mimicking your deepest regrets!
But it sounds just like him!
Elara, snap out of it! If you step off the path, you'll be lost forever.
Elara stumbled, drawn toward the ethereal voice drifting through the fog.
By the gods, hold still!
Alaric grabbed her arm, pulling her back to the stony trail just as the fog parted, revealing a sheer drop into a chasm.
I... I almost stepped right off.
Told you. The woods don't like visitors.
Thank you, Alaric. You saved me.
Just don't do it again. My heart's too old for this kind of stress.
Days turned into weeks, until finally, the imposing shadow of the Obsidian Keep loomed before them.
Look at the size of that thing. The walls are solid black stone.
And guarded by the undead. We can't fight our way through the main gate.
There's a drainage pipe on the eastern wall. It's how the old kings supplied the fortress during sieges.
How do you know that?
I used to guard this place, back when it was a royal outpost.
Lead the way.
They slipped silently through the muck of the tunnels, avoiding the shambling corpses that patrolled the courtyards.
We need to head to the central spire. That's where the ritual chamber is.
I sense an immense darkness above us. The crown is near.
Throwing open the massive iron doors, they stepped into a chamber lit by sickly green fire.
Ah, the disgraced knight and the little weed. I was wondering when you would arrive.
Malakor. Hand over the crown.
Or what? You'll strike me down with your rusted blade? I have conquered death itself!
You pervert the natural order! The earth rejects you!
The earth will be my footstool! Rise, my servants, and dispose of these insects.
Skeletons burst from the stone floor, armed with ancient weapons.
I'll handle the bones! You deal with the sorcerer!
Alaric charged into the fray, his broadsword shattering the undead with mighty swings.
Winds of the storm, hear my plea! Strike down this abomination!
Lightning crackled from Elara's fingertips, striking Malakor's magical shield.
Pathetic! You lack the power of a true Arch-Druid!
Hey, ugly! Catch!
Alaric hurled a shield he wrenched from a skeleton, striking Malakor in the face and breaking his concentration.
Insolent fool! I will flay the skin from your bones!
Now's my chance! The crown is exposed on the pedestal!
Run for it, Elara! I'll hold him back!
Alaric tackled the sorcerer, pinning his arms to prevent him from casting spells.
Get off me, you brute!
Goddess of the earth, shatter this dark artifact!
Elara slammed her wooden staff onto the Obsidian Crown. With a blinding flash of green light, the crown shattered into a thousand pieces.
No! My power! My glorious power!
Without the crown's magic, Malakor rapidly aged, crumbling into dust beneath Alaric's hands.
Well, that was thoroughly unpleasant.
It's over. The dead are returning to their rest.
You did it, kid. You avenged your master and saved the realm.
We did it, Alaric. You're a hero.
Don't go spreading that rumor around. It ruins my image.
What will you do now?
I think I might go back to the Prancing Boar. Gromm owes me an ale.
As dawn broke over the mountains, casting a golden light on the ruins, a new era of peace began.
